techs.name: Hello World
techs.quote: "Hello, World!" is the traditional first program of a new language. Print the greeting, and the journey begins.

techs.name: Binary System
techs.quote: A method of counting and carrying. There are only two digits, 0 and 1, and one digit is carried for every 2. It is mostly used in electronic computers.

techs.name: Boolean Algebra
techs.quote: Boolean algebra is the branch of algebra in which the values of the variables are true and false, usually denoted 1 and 0, and the operations are AND, OR, and NOT.

techs.name: Babbage Engine
techs.quote: Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine (1837) was the first general-purpose mechanical computer design, with a store, a mill, and punched-card input.

techs.name: Sequential Structure
techs.quote: Sequential structure is the simplest and most commonly used program structure, as long as the corresponding statements are written in the order of solving the problem. Its execution order is top-down and sequential.

techs.name: Von Neumann System
techs.quote: Von Neumann system: The number system of digital computers adopts binary and computers should execute programs in sequence.

techs.name: Selection Structure
techs.quote: The core of selection structure is to form conditional judgments through relational expressions and logical expressions, and the result is determined by Boolean values to determine the branch path.

techs.name: Iteration Structure
techs.quote: Iteration structure refers to a program structure that needs to be repeatedly executed to determine whether to continue or exit the loop based on the conditions in the loop body.

techs.name: Function
techs.quote: A function is a block of organized, reusable code that is used to perform a single, related action. Functions provide better modularity for your application and a high degree of code reusing.

techs.name: Linear Algebra
techs.quote: Linear algebra is the branch of mathematics concerning linear equations, linear functions, and their representations through matrices and vector spaces.

techs.name: Turing Machine
techs.quote: Alan Turing's 1936 abstract machine formalized computation and showed that some problems are undecidable.

techs.name: Code
techs.quote: Code is a set of instructions written in a programming language that a computer can understand and execute.

techs.name: Basic Algorithm
techs.quote: The algorithm describes a process in which a computation can start from an initial state and initial input, go through a series of finite and clearly defined states, and ultimately produce an output that stops at a final state.

techs.name: Array
techs.quote: An array is a data structure that contains a group of elements. Typically, these elements are all of the same data type, such as an integer or string.

techs.name: Computer Architecture
techs.quote: Pipelining, caching, and superscalar execution shaped the design of modern processors.

techs.name: Character String
techs.quote: A string is a sequence of characters, either as a literal constant or as some kind of variable. The latter may allow its elements to be mutated and the length changed, or it may be fixed (after creation).

techs.name: Pointer
techs.quote: A pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another variable. Pointers are used to manipulate data in memory directly.

techs.name: Discrete Mathematics
techs.quote: Discrete mathematics is the study of mathematical structures that are fundamentally discrete rather than continuous, including graphs, sets, and logic.

techs.name: Circuit Principles
techs.quote: Circuit principles describe how logic gates are built from transistors and combined into the integrated circuits at the heart of every computer.

techs.name: Computability Theory
techs.quote: The Church-Turing thesis established that all reasonable models of computation are equivalent.

techs.name: Hash Table
techs.quote: A hash table maps keys to values with a hash function, giving average constant-time lookup.

techs.name: Memory Architecture
techs.quote: The memory architecture covers the connection mode between storage devices and computer systems, and has developed through bus storage, storage networks, and virtual storage stages.

techs.name: Algorithm Complexity
techs.quote: Big-O notation and complexity classes compare algorithms by how their resource use grows with input.

techs.name: Stack and Queue
techs.quote: A stack is a linear data structure that follows the Last In First Out (LIFO) principle, while a queue follows the First In First Out (FIFO) principle.

techs.name: Graph Theory
techs.quote: Graph theory studies vertices and edges, providing the language for networks, routes, and dependencies.

techs.name: Logic Synthesis
techs.quote: Logic synthesis automates the translation of Boolean specifications into gate-level circuits.

techs.name: Complexity Theory
techs.quote: Complexity theory classifies problems by the resources needed to solve them, from P and NP to PSPACE.

techs.name: Database Theory
techs.quote: Database theory formalizes relations, transactions, and query languages for reliable data storage.

techs.name: Memory Release
techs.quote: Memory release refers to the technical means of releasing data residing in memory to improve the utilization and performance of system memory resources.

techs.name: Dynamic Programming
techs.quote: Dynamic programming solves complex problems by combining solutions to overlapping subproblems.

techs.name: Recursive Algorithms
techs.quote: Recursion solves a problem by reducing it to smaller instances of the same problem.

techs.name: Information Theory
techs.quote: Shannon's information theory quantifies information, compression, and channel capacity.

techs.name: NP-Completeness
techs.quote: NP-completeness identifies the hardest problems in NP, whose solutions can be checked in polynomial time.

techs.name: VLSI Design
techs.quote: VLSI design packs millions of transistors onto a single chip through hierarchical circuit design.

techs.name: Database Systems
techs.quote: Database systems implement storage engines, transactions, and query processing.

techs.name: Operating System
techs.quote: An operating system (OS) is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides common services for computer programs.

techs.name: Compiler Theory
techs.quote: Compiler theory formalized parsing, optimization, and code generation from high-level languages to machine code.

techs.name: Class and Object
techs.quote: A class is a blueprint for creating objects, providing initial values for state (member variables or attributes), and implementations of behavior (member functions or methods).

techs.name: Internet
techs.quote: The Internet, also known as the Net, is a global system of interconnected computer networks that use the Internet protocol suite (TCP/IP) to communicate between networks and devices.

techs.name: Cryptography
techs.quote: Public-key cryptography made secure communication possible over untrusted networks.

techs.name: Processor Architecture
techs.quote: Processor architecture refers to the design and organization of a computer's central processing unit (CPU), including its instruction set, data paths, and control unit.

techs.name: Distributed Databases
techs.quote: Distributed databases replicate and partition data across multiple machines.

techs.name: Virtualization
techs.quote: Virtualization lets one physical machine host many isolated virtual machines.

techs.name: JIT Compilation
techs.quote: Just-in-time compilation translates bytecode to machine code while a program runs.

techs.name: Design Patterns
techs.quote: Design patterns capture reusable solutions to recurring object-oriented design problems.

techs.name: Website
techs.quote: A website is a collection of web pages and related content that is identified by a common domain name and published on at least one web server.

techs.name: Network Protocol
techs.quote: A network protocol is a set of rules and conventions for communication between network devices. It defines how data is formatted, transmitted, and received over a network.

techs.name: Cybersecurity
techs.quote: As networks spread, security became a discipline of firewalls, encryption, and intrusion detection.

techs.name: Assembly Language
techs.quote: Assembly language is a low-level programming language that uses symbolic code and is specific to a computer architecture. It is converted into machine language using an assembler.

techs.name: Big Data
techs.quote: Big data technologies process datasets too large for a single machine.

techs.name: Cloud Computing
techs.quote: Cloud computing delivers computing resources over a network on demand.

techs.name: Bytecode
techs.quote: Bytecode is an intermediate instruction set executed by a virtual machine.

techs.name: Software Architecture
techs.quote: Software architecture defines the structure and interactions of a large software system.

techs.name: Web Frameworks
techs.quote: Web frameworks provide reusable structure for building web applications.

techs.name: Peer-to-Peer
techs.quote: Peer-to-peer networks let nodes share resources without a central server.

techs.name: Zero Trust Security
techs.quote: Zero trust security assumes no implicit trust and verifies every request.

techs.name: Machine Language
techs.quote: Machine language is the set of binary instructions a processor can execute directly, the lowest level of programming.

techs.name: Data Science
techs.quote: Data science combines statistics, programming, and domain knowledge to extract insight from data.

techs.name: Cloud Native
techs.quote: Cloud-native software is designed for containers, orchestration, and elastic scaling.

techs.name: WebAssembly
techs.quote: WebAssembly is a portable binary format that runs near-native code in the browser.

techs.name: Microservices
techs.quote: Microservices split an application into independently deployable services.

techs.name: Internet of Things
techs.quote: The Internet of Things connects everyday devices to networks and each other.

techs.name: Blockchain
techs.quote: The 2008 Bitcoin whitepaper introduced a distributed ledger secured by cryptography and proof-of-work.

techs.name: Parallel Computing
techs.quote: Parallel computing executes many operations simultaneously to reduce wall-clock time.

techs.name: Machine Learning
techs.quote: Machine learning builds models that improve from data instead of relying only on hand-written rules.

techs.name: Serverless Computing
techs.quote: Serverless computing runs functions on demand without managing servers.

techs.name: WebGPU
techs.quote: WebGPU exposes modern graphics and compute capabilities to the browser.

techs.name: Container Orchestration
techs.quote: Container orchestration schedules, scales, and heals containerized services.

techs.name: Edge Computing
techs.quote: Edge computing moves computation close to data sources to reduce latency.

techs.name: Consensus Algorithms
techs.quote: Consensus algorithms let distributed nodes agree on a shared state.

techs.name: GPU Computing
techs.quote: GPU computing uses massively parallel graphics processors for general computation.

techs.name: Deep Learning
techs.quote: Deep neural networks and backpropagation brought breakthroughs in vision, speech, and language.

techs.name: Large Language Models
techs.quote: Large language models learn statistical patterns from vast text corpora.

techs.name: Artificial Intelligence
techs.quote: The 1956 Dartmouth workshop founded artificial intelligence as a field of computer science.

techs.name: Computer Graphics
techs.quote: Computer graphics turned linear algebra into images, from rasterization and shading to ray tracing.

techs.name: Infrastructure as Code
techs.quote: Infrastructure as code manages servers and networks through versioned configuration.

techs.name: Computer Vision
techs.quote: Computer vision teaches machines to interpret images, from edge detection to convolutional networks.

techs.name: Smart Contracts
techs.quote: Smart contracts encode agreements as self-executing programs on a blockchain.

techs.name: Distributed Training
techs.quote: Distributed training splits model training across many machines and accelerators.

techs.name: AutoML
techs.quote: AutoML automates model selection, hyperparameter tuning, and architecture search.

techs.name: Neuromorphic Computing
techs.quote: Neuromorphic computing mimics the brain's spiking neurons in hardware.

techs.name: Natural Language Processing
techs.quote: Natural language processing taught computers to parse, translate, and generate human language.

techs.name: Brain-Computer Interface
techs.quote: Brain-computer interfaces read neural signals and translate them into commands.

techs.name: Metaverse
techs.quote: The metaverse is a persistent shared virtual world.

techs.name: Self-Healing Systems
techs.quote: Self-healing systems detect and recover from failures automatically.

techs.name: Autonomous Systems
techs.quote: Autonomous systems make decisions without continuous human control.

techs.name: Zero-Knowledge Proofs
techs.quote: Zero-knowledge proofs convince a verifier of a statement without revealing the secret.

techs.name: Federated Learning
techs.quote: Federated learning trains models across devices without centralizing their data.

techs.name: Quantum Computing
techs.quote: Quantum computers exploit superposition and entanglement to solve certain problems exponentially faster than classical machines.

techs.name: Artificial General Intelligence
techs.quote: AGI would match or exceed human intelligence across a broad range of tasks.

techs.name: Autonomic Computing
techs.quote: Autonomic computing systems manage and tune themselves.

techs.name: Extended Reality
techs.quote: Extended reality combines virtual and augmented reality with physical space.

techs.name: Formal Verification
techs.quote: Formal methods use logic and proof to show that hardware and software meet their specifications.

techs.name: Post-Quantum Cryptography
techs.quote: Post-quantum cryptography designs algorithms that remain secure against attacks by quantum computers.

techs.name: Swarm Robotics
techs.quote: Swarm robotics coordinates many simple robots into collective behavior.

techs.name: Future Tech
techs.quote: The future is not yet written. Keep researching to see what comes next.
